title: The Discharging Base for Planar Graphs

problemStatement.plain: Prove, axiom-free, the discharging-base inequality ∑(6 − deg v) ≥ 12 that underlies the Five Color Theorem's low-degree-vertex fact, and derive its sharpened consequences (≥2 vertices of degree ≤ 5, no minimum degree ≥ 6, average degree < 6).

insights: The charge 6 − deg(v) is the discrete Gauss–Bonnet curvature; handshaking + Euler force its total to the constant 6V − 2E ≥ 12.
The parent Five Color Theorem's exists_low_degree is the weakest corollary of the discharging base (positive total ⟹ positive term).
Separating the planarity-free charge identity from the planar inequality makes the equality/sharpness case (triangulations) fall out for free.
builtItems: discharging_base: ∑(6 − deg v) ≥ 12 for planar graphs
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has no planar-graph definition; the edge bound E ≤ 3V − 6 is taken as an explicit hypothesis (as in the parent file).
nextSteps: Push the low-degree count from ≥2 to the classical ≥3 via structural/recursive charge accounting.
Generalize the charge identity to surfaces of genus g via the Euler characteristic 2 − 2g.
